span.label: mechanisms

span.label: mechanisms

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Faster membrane time constants combined with strong thalamocortical synaptic drive make PV+ cells fire early, placing them in a feedforward inhibitory loop that sharpens the timing of pyramidal responses

span.label: PV+ cells densely sample a small radius, so their tuning should mirror how the local network is organised - broad where tuning is salt-and-pepper, narrow where it is columnar

span.label: cotuned inhibition sharpens spike tuning through a thresholding or iceberg mechanism rather than by suppressing non-preferred stimuli

span.label: RETRACTED (THE `because` INTRODUCES A PREMISE, AND THE EDGE READS IT AS A CONSEQUENCE) · local pooling —causes→ tonotopically
span.note: RETRACTED: THE `because` INTRODUCES A PREMISE, AND THE EDGE READS IT AS A CONSEQUENCE. The edge is `local pooling --causes--> tonotopically`. The span: 'Quotation withheld that PV+ cells, like PV- cells, will be well tuned to an area's preferred frequency.' Tonotopy is a BACKGROUND FACT the hypothesis is applied to; it is the given, not the product. Local pooling does not organise the cortex tonotopically - the tonotopy is what makes the pooling hypothesis yield a testable prediction about TUNING. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): that a known organisation plus a hypothesis yields a prediction, and the prediction is about tuning width, not about tonotopy. That is the sibling edge [2] `local pooling --causes--> tuning width`, which was READ IN THE SAME PASS AND LEFT - it has the prediction and the confirming result ('we found that the frequency tuning widths of PV+ and PV- cells were not significantly different'). So nothing is kept here; the content is already carried by the edge next to it. — strength of the relation: 1 — THE PREDICTION REVERSES ACROSS MODALITIES: the same pooling principle makes PV+ cells broadly tuned in salt-and-pepper mouse V1 and well tuned in columnar auditory cortex
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: local pooling —causes→ tuning width
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — MECHANISM: dense sampling of a small radius means the cell inherits whatever tuning organisation that radius has - so a tonotopic area predicts well-tuned inhibitory cells

span.label: RETRACTED (A PREDICTION CONFIRMED BY A NULL, RECORDED AS A CONTRAST) · PV+ —contrasted-with→ PV−
span.note: RETRACTED: A PREDICTION CONFIRMED BY A NULL, RECORDED AS A CONTRAST. The edge is `PV+ --contrasted-with--> PV−`, weight 0.4. The span: 'the local pooling hypothesis PREDICTS that PV+ cells, LIKE PV− cells, will be well tuned to an area's preferred frequency. CONSISTENT WITH THIS, we found that Quotation withheld.' The sentence contains the word `like`, the phrase `consistent with this`, and a null - three signals that the two cell types are being shown to MATCH. The edge's own note says 'the contrast the paper looked for is absent, and its absence is the finding', and then asserts the contrast anyway. THE NULL RESULT HAD NOWHERE TO GO. The schema has `contrasted-with` and `distinct-from` for a difference and `same-as` for an identity, and NOTHING FOR 'THE DIFFERENCE WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT FOUND'. So the nearest positive type was chosen, the truth was written into `note`, and `weight` was lowered - which is this project's own thesis committed inside its own layer: the missing vocabulary did not produce a gap in the data, IT PRODUCED A VALUE IN THE WRONG FIELD. A join reads the type; it does not read the note, and it cannot distinguish a low weight meaning 'weak evidence' from one meaning 'the opposite of what I said'. Q-388. — strength of the relation: 0.4 — the record marks this weak — WEIGHT LOW ON PURPOSE: tuning widths did NOT differ - the contrast the paper looked for is absent, and its absence is the finding
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.note: RETRACTED: THE `to` ENDPOINT IS AN ADVERB. The edge is `auditory cortex --part-of--> tonotopically`. The span: 'Quotation withheld...' A cortex cannot be part of `tonotopically`. What the clause states is a PROPERTY of the cortex - that its organisation is tonotopic - and the tagger took the adverb as if it named a thing. Same shape as the `trend`, `terminology` and `classification` endpoints retracted earlier today: A WORD THAT IS NOT A NOUN PHRASE CANNOT BE AN ENDPOINT. Found by the neighbour query (Q-400). span.label: Frequency tuning width did not differ significantly between optogenetically identified PV+ interneurons and PV- neurons in mouse auditory cortex (0.84 vs 0.62 octaves), unlike the broad orientation tuning reported for PV+ cells in mouse visual cortex.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Very tightly tuned cells (below 0.5 octaves) were about half as common among PV+ cells (29%) as among PV- cells (58%), even though the two distributions largely overlapped.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The best frequency of every tuned PV+ neuron was within half an octave of its recording site's best frequency, so PV+ tuning matched the local population.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: PV+ cells responded to best-frequency tones roughly 11 ms earlier than PV- cells (17.9 vs 29.1 ms).

span.label: The latency advantage was stimulus-specific: for white noise, PV+ and PV- latencies did not differ significantly.

span.label: PV+ cells fired at twice the spontaneous rate (5.5 vs 2.0 Hz) and twice the sound-evoked rate (30.3 vs 14.5 Hz) of PV- cells.

span.label: After normalizing for their higher firing rates, PV+ cells had shallower response gain to characteristic-frequency tones than PV- cells (0.04 vs 0.15).

span.label: PV+ cells were markedly less intensity-tuned than PV- cells for tones at characteristic frequency: only 14% of PV+ cells were nonmonotonic compared with 55% of PV- cells.

span.label: For white noise, where the two groups were equally monotonic, the gain and dynamic-range differences disappeared, indicating the gain difference follows from monotonicity rather than being an independent property.

span.label: Classifying cells by extracellular spike waveform instead of by PV expression would misclassify as many as 40% of them, so waveform is an unreliable marker of PV+ identity.
